title: DEIM-S vs RT-DETR-R18: benchmark on the same protocol
dek: Measured on the same COCO protocol: DEIM-S leads by 2.3 mAP points with fewer parameters, but RT-DETR-R18 is 29.37% faster on desktop GPU.
author: Vision Analysis

blocks.text: DEIM-S is the more accurate model: 52.1 vs 49.8 mAP@50-95 against RT-DETR-R18 on an RTX 5070 Ti in PyTorch, and it reaches that with fewer parameters (10.32M vs 20.18M) and less VRAM (142 vs 169 MB). RT-DETR-R18 is the faster detector on that GPU: 47.2 vs 33.4 FPS, a 29.37% edge. The speed order flips on Raspberry Pi 5, where DEIM-S pulls ahead. Pick by deployment target.

DEIM-S (10.32M parameters, Apache-2.0) and RT-DETR-R18 (20.18M, Apache-2.0) both evaluate at 640 px input, so the input resolution matches and does not skew the comparison. DEIM-S is the smaller model here. Both have verified rows on desktop GPU, Jetson Orin, and Raspberry Pi 5, so this comparison covers the deploy targets where the answer changes.

blocks.caption: Accuracy vs parameters on COCO val2017. DEIM-S and RT-DETR-R18 highlighted against the full set.

blocks.text: mAP is shown in percent form. DEIM-S measures 52.1 mAP@50-95 to RT-DETR-R18's 49.8, a 2.3 point lead. The gap is wider on small objects: 36.0 vs 32.7 mAP_small, a 10.11% relative difference. DEIM-S reaches that accuracy with fewer parameters than RT-DETR-R18.
On the RTX 5070 Ti, RT-DETR-R18 runs 47.2 FPS to DEIM-S's 33.4 in PyTorch, a 29.37% edge. The gap holds under conversion: 92.5 vs 67.5 FPS on ONNX Runtime, 120.6 vs 97.6 FPS on TensorRT FP32.

The speed verdict does not travel to CPU. On Raspberry Pi 5, DEIM-S runs 1.1 FPS to RT-DETR-R18's 0.8. On Jetson Orin the two tie at 10.2 FPS. If your target is a bare Pi, the desktop numbers point the wrong way.

Pick DEIM-S when accuracy or memory matters, or when the target is a Raspberry Pi where it is the faster detector: it is more accurate at every object size and uses less VRAM. Pick RT-DETR-R18 for desktop or server GPU throughput, where it leads on every GPU runtime measured. Both ship under Apache-2.0, so licensing does not force the choice.

# pip install libreyolo
from libreyolo import LibreYOLO

deim = LibreYOLO("LibreDEIMs.pt")        # 10.32M params, 52.1 mAP@50-95
rtdetr = LibreYOLO("LibreRTDETRr18.pt")  # 20.18M params, 49.8 mAP@50-95

results = deim("image.jpg")
